tools.name: medusa.get_stock
tools.description: Read one SKU's stock at every location the store can sell from, straight from the ERP. Per location: stocked_quantity (units counted there), reserved_quantity (held for open orders) and available_quantity (stocked minus reserved, what can still be sold); has_level false means the SKU has no inventory level at that location yet, so its zeros are not a counted zero. This reads current stock only: it never changes it. An unknown SKU is a not_found error; a SKU that exists but cannot hold stock here is an invalid_arguments error whose message carries the ERP's code (ambiguous_sku: several variants share it; not_inventory_managed; kit_variant: stock lives on the kit's parts; fba_listing: Amazon holds the stock). Relay that reason to the user and do not propose stock for the SKU.

tools.name: medusa.propose_stock_changes
tools.description: Propose stock changes; a human confirms them in the ERP. Two kinds of line. kind "set" sets one SKU's stocked quantity at a location (quantity, and expected_stocked_quantity: the stocked quantity there now, read it with medusa.get_stock; 0 when the SKU has no level at that location yet; a set line without it is refused). kind "adjust" is a relative change (delta: a signed non-zero integer, e.g. 12 received or -3 broken) with a reason: received, damaged, count_correction or other (other needs a reason_note saying what happened); it is applied to the stock as it is when a human confirms, so it needs no expected_stocked_quantity, and a missing reason refuses that line. Use set for a counted total and adjust for a movement the merchant described. This never changes stock: quantities take effect only after a human confirms the batch in the ERP at batch.erp_url. Afterwards tell the user "N lines awaiting confirmation" (N is batch.counts.proposed) and give them batch.erp_url; report every refused[] line with its reason and every line warning (large_jump, active_fbm_listing) as the ERP wrote them, and never say stock was updated. A source is required and is checked before anything is sent: kind "user" with a reference that quotes the merchant's own words and when or on what occasion they said them (e.g. "Mia, 2 Oct 14:00, counting the shelf: 150 pcs"), or kind "sheet" with a reference citing the file and row (e.g. "stock-2026-10.xlsx row 12"). Never invent or estimate a quantity, and never use kind "agent": your own inference is not a source, so when the merchant has not said or written the number, ask. If every line is refused nothing is stored. Read the result back later with medusa.get_stock_change.

tools.name: medusa.get_stock_change
tools.description: Read one stock-change batch by batch_id: its source, per-status line counts and every line with its status (proposed, confirmed, rejected, stale or expired), warnings, and current stocked/reserved/available quantity at the line's location. A proposed line has not changed any stock: quantities take effect only after a human confirms the batch in the ERP, so send the user the batch's erp_url (the review page) and say how many lines are still waiting for confirmation. Never claim stock was updated while a line is proposed. An unknown batch_id is a not_found error.

tools.description: Fetch Medusa products with their status and trimmed variants. Provide exactly one of product_id or sku.

tools.name: host.open_url
tools.description: This host's own browser: open a URL in a tab the user can see. Host tool, not an Intgral MCP tool.
